the highest concentrations of Hg in hakes of the GoL are due to the combination of higher bioavailability, slower growth, and higher trophic position of this population.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the bioenergetic approach is an effective and simple tool to understand and predict Hg biomagnification in food webs.
the trophic position and growth rate of hakes are important factors to explain the differences in MeHg concentrations between the two studied hake populations.
the bioaccumulation of MeHg in hake muscle is controlled by the combined effects of trophic position and growth, which in turn are influenced by environmental conditions.
